MeshGroup hierarchy equivalence: layout and geometric answers

The public group promises a collection of bounded member surfaces and
nearest ray/surface answers. Members returns placements without exposing
its mutable slice; it does not promise the caller's input order, and the
constructor already permutes members while splitting. Exact ties between
equidistant surfaces do not prescribe which component wins.

Each surviving split variant still permutes all input indices, keeps
members and boxes aligned, partitions a nonempty range into two nonempty
ranges, and unions the same child/member boxes. Leaf cutoffs 3/4/5 and the
one-third median retain a finite hierarchy. Axis and sort-direction choices
change partition shape, not membership or any bound's enclosed geometry.
The sort with <= may order equal centres differently, but every sorting
operation still permutes indices and the recursion remains range-bounded.

The pruning removals do more member tests, but preserve the same finite
candidate set and use each exact member hitter's original near/far window.
Nearest >= at equal box distance can skip only candidates no closer than
the current best; changing strict improvement to <= chooses another tied
nearest component. All valid tied components satisfy the geometric promise.

These operations change performance/layout and unspecified tie choice,
not promised geometry. Go group nodes are not the GPU hierarchy: GPU
encoding rebuilds its own sorted hierarchy from Members. Keep this limit
explicit; this is not an assertion that all variants have equal speed.

The NewMeshGroup count>0 to >=0 change only adds CornerNormals(0) for an
empty nonnil mesh. A public zero Mesh is flat, so CornerNormals returns
false before indexing. A nonempty smooth Mesh comes only from New, which
already requires faces. The later zero-count guard still refuses emptiness.
